scoreNote: Strong-adequate (4.5): grants that fresh imagination can outrun fixed habits, then argues experience is equally vital; two developed examples with analysis, controlled prose on a memorable First and Second skeleton.

sentences.text: We often admire fresh, imaginative people while also trusting those with years of experience.
One claim holds that imagination is more valuable than experience, on the reason that inexperienced people are free to imagine what is possible without old habits holding them back.
I agree that imagination is precious, but I disagree that it is generally more valuable than experience.

sections.role: Body 1 — The truth in the reason

sentences.text: First, there is real truth in the reason behind the claim.
People without experience are sometimes free to imagine bold ideas that experts quickly dismiss.
For example, a newcomer may suggest a fresh solution simply because she does not know it is supposed to be impossible.
This shows that imagination can break through the fixed habits that experience sometimes creates.
Old assumptions can blind experienced people to new and better ways of doing things.
Imagination is what allows anyone to picture a future different from the past.
To this extent, the claim rightly values the power of a free imagination.
Second, however, experience is just as valuable as imagination, and often more so.
Experience teaches which ideas actually work and which ones quietly fail.
Consider a surgeon whose years of practice let her handle a crisis no imagination alone could solve.
Such skill shows that real knowledge, gained over time, can save lives and prevent disasters.
Imagination without experience can produce exciting ideas that collapse the moment they are tested.
The greatest results usually come when a vivid imagination is guided by hard-won experience.
Experience, then, is not the enemy of imagination but its necessary partner.
In conclusion, imagination is genuinely valuable and can free us from old habits.
But experience is equally vital, since it shows which imagined ideas can truly work.
The most valuable thinkers combine a bold imagination with the wisdom that only experience provides.
